statement: Combined capex of the 5 largest spenders falls year on year for 2 consecutive quarters (securities filings; by 2028-06-30)
status_at_phase_end: Not met; far from it. Combined quarterly capex of the four largest Bloc A spenders grew ~62-67% year on year in each 2025 quarter reported in-phase (Q1 $71.9B, Q2 $88.2B, Q3 $97.3B). All guided higher for 2026. A fifth-ranked Bloc A spender raised its fiscal-year capex guidance to ~$50B (Dec). Risk signals emerged late in the year: that spender's shares fell ~11-13% on spending and cash burn, its credit-default-swap spread hit a 16-year high, and 'AI bubble' worries became mainstream. Even so, there was no quarter-on-year decline.

items.summary: After Q4 2024 results, the four largest Bloc A cloud/platform spenders guided ~$320B combined 2025 capex (vs ~$230B in 2024), despite a Bloc B low-cost model raising efficiency questions.

items.summary: A fifth-ranked Bloc A spender raised fiscal-year capex guidance to ~$50B (from $35B in September; prior fiscal year $21.2B). Quarterly capex was ~$12B (vs $8.5B). Free cash flow was about -$10B and debt ~$106B.
items.detail: Oracle FY26 Q2 results (2025-12-10), CFO Kehring; CNBC 2025-12-10; Bloomberg via BusinessLine 2025-12-12.

items.summary: That spender's shares fell ~11-13%, its five-year credit default swap spread hit the highest level since 2009, and AI-related stocks sold off on doubts about how fast AI capex pays back. This is the first market signal of financing strain that could later force spending cuts.
items.detail: Reuters 2025-12-11 'Oracle slumps as gloomy forecasts, soaring spending fan AI bubble worries'; ICE Data Services CDS ~1.41pp.

items.summary: Q4 2025 figures were published only in 2026 (excluded by the as-of rule). The indicator also needs a fixed five-firm list and capex definition (cash property and equipment vs including finance leases; non-calendar fiscal years).
